content.text: Found it. The commit `9501cccdbbeec3a4940dee8532b143ad5febe7c8` introduced the buggy merged condition, replacing the previous correct code (which only handled `nonCombat`) with a combined `||` condition that incorrectly plays `CLIP_PHASE_MOVE_NONCOMBAT` for both combat and non-combat moves.

delta.text: ding: prior to this commit, the code correctly used an `if/else if` to play `CLIP_PHASE_MOVE_NONCOMBAT` for non-combat moves and `CLIP_PHASE
_MOVE_COMBAT` for combat moves. This commit merged the two branches into a single `if` with an `||` condition, but kept only the `CLIP_PHAS
E_MOVE_NONCOMBAT` sound and only updated `m_soundPlayedAlreadyNonCombatMove` — losing the combat-move sound and never setting `m_soundPl
ayedAlreadyCombatMove`. This is exactly the bug that `b1c9edc39` fixes (by splitting the condition back into two `if` blocks, though it left the `CLIP_P
HASE_MOVE_NONCOMBAT` sound in the combat branch, which appears to be its own residual/incomplete fix, but that's outside the scope of finding the introducing
er.java` to trace the line-level history of the buggy condition (`if ((nonCombat && !m_soundPlayedAlreadyNonCombatMove) || (!nonCombat && !m_soundPlayedAlre

adyCombatMove))`) shown in the fix diff. This traces exactly which commit introduced each version of those lines.

**(2) Specific change:** Commit `9501cccdb
beec3a4940dee8532b143ad5febe7c8` ("Remove DefaultSoundChannel playLocal sound method...") refactored the `move()` method in
lreadyCombatMove = true` flag update, so during a combat move phase the wrong sound (`CLIP_PHASE_MOVE_NONCOMBAT`) was played and the combat-move "already played" flag was never set (caus

ing the wrong sound to replay every turn as well).

**(3) Evidence:** The `git log -L` output directly shows this line-history: the
correct if/else-if logic existed before `9501cccd`, was replaced by the buggy merged condition in `9501cccd`, persisted un
changed through `434f9988` (only a parameter-type refactor, not touching the logic), and was finally corrected in the target
fix commit `b1c9edc39`, which restores two independent `if` blocks. There is no intervening commit that touches these specific lines between `
9501cccd` and `b1c9edc39`, so `9501cccd` is the sole bug-introducing commit. I have high confidence in this conclusion given the direct line-blame trail
